calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Predators’ net
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Senators have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Predators near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Senators’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.
calls.call: The Senators get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.

calls.head: Bruisers vs. Finesse
calls.body: On physicality, Ottawa is one of the league’s best, but Nashville is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Expect most of the big hits to come from the Senators.

surprises.head: Nashville brought the hits
surprises.body: Nashville is one of the league’s lightest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 175 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 84 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 100 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Stützle sparks the Senators back from two down
paras: The Predators’ Matt Murray was back in an NHL net for the first time since Jan 8, 2024. Ross Colton scored his first goal for Nashville midway through the first to open the scoring. Jonathan Marchessault stretched the lead to 2-0 on the power play less than five minutes later. Tim Stützle got the Senators on the board on the power play midway through the second. The Senators went more than 22 minutes without a shot on goal, from midway through the second to late in the third, even with a power play in that stretch. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season. With the goalie pulled and less than two minutes left, Drake Batherson tied it 2-2 for Ottawa. Stützle and Shane Pinto scored in the shootout for the Senators. The Preds’ Vitali Pinchuk played his first NHL game and picked up a point.

The Senators had the better of the chances. Linus Ullmark made 16 saves for the Senators. The Senators moved to 4-1-0 but slipped out of first in the Atlantic, while the Predators fell to 2-1-2, fifth in the Central.

items.text: Tim Stützle passed Radek Bonk for eighth on the Senators’ all-time goals list, with 153.
Steven Stamkos has a point in every game this season.
Jonathan Marchessault scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 2 (ten games played since).
Jayden Struble made his Predators debut, after four seasons with the Canadiens.
